encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue, fever, and persistent cough over one month

lines: Progressive fatigue, fever, and persistent cough over one month

The patient returns to the Emergency Department with progressive respiratory symptoms in the context of his severe alcohol use disorder, Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, and history of scurvy and Wernicke encephalopathy.
He reports night sweats, decreased appetite, and a 7-kg (15-lb) unintentional weight loss.
The cough is occasionally productive of dark-tinged sputum, and he has felt increasingly weak and short of breath.
He denies recent travel or known sick contacts.

He is currently living in a homeless shelter and has a history of chronic alcohol use.
Temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), blood pressure is 100/64 mm Hg, pulse is 108/min, and respiratory rate is 22/min.
On examination, the patient appears thin and fatigued.
He has dry mucous membranes, coarse breath sounds in the upper posterior lung zones, and no peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy.
Laboratory evaluation shows normocytic anemia and mildly elevated liver enzymes.
A sputum stain reveals acid-fast bacilli organized in a serpentine pattern.

lines: Several weeks of worsening cough, fever, and foul-smputum after heavy drinking and vomiting
The patient returns with worsening cough and fever, six months after tuberculosis treatment, in the setting of heavy alcohol use and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
He describes the sputum as thick and putrid, occasionally blood-tinged, and notes that his symptoms began after a night of heavy drinking during which he vomited multiple times.
He denies any recent travel, tuberculosis exposure, or known immunodeficiency, but reports ongoing fatigue, weight loss, and pleuritic chest pain.

He has a long-standing history of alcoholism and frequently falls asleep in a supine position while intoxicated.
On examination, he appears cachectic and mildly diaphoretic.
Breath sounds are decreased at the right lung base with dullness to percussion and occasional crackles.
Chest imaging reveals a cavitary lesion with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe, consistent with a lung abscess.
Bronchoalveolar lavage is performed, and anaerobic cultures grow Bacteroides spp .
